title: Setup words

walkthroughs.title: Every setup carries a plan
steps: Every trade plan we teach hands you two prices: the trigger, which is the entry, and the stop.
R is your risk per share, entry to stop. A third comes off at 3R and another at 5R.
Then you trail. The stop follows the stock up, under each higher low or a rising average.

walkthroughs.title: Names and families
steps: Our catalog sorts every setup into a family. Learn the family and the name gets easier to place.
The Kicker, High Volume Edge and Gap Support are Gaps & Catalysts. Oops Reversal and Slingshot are Reversals & Reclaims.
The Launchpad sits in Bases & Breakouts. The Go Signal and the ORB are Intraday.

walkthroughs.title: A name is not an edge
steps: The textbook kicker is a down candle, then a gap up the other way.
Investopedia calls it highly reliable. Bulkowski's tests found it reversed the trend 53% of the time, almost random.
So I don't trade the name. I trade the plan: our entry, our stop, a third off at 3R and at 5R.

questions.q: In our setup plans, what is a setup's trigger?
questions.why: The setup's entry price. In our plans, trigger means entry. Each setup's detector returns its own trigger and its own stop for the candle it fires on. The trigger is a price on the chart. It is not the stop, not a profit target, and not the news behind the move. The trims come later, at 3R and 5R, measured off your entry-to-stop risk.
questions.lesson_line: Trigger means entry. Every setup hands you one, plus a stop.

wrong.The setup's stop price: The stop is the other price each setup gives you. The trigger is where you get in.
wrong.The first profit target: Trims come later: a third at 3R and a third at 5R, measured off your entry-to-stop risk.
wrong.The news that moved it: News can be why a stock moves. The trigger is a price on the chart.

questions.simple: The trigger is the entry price, the spot where you get in, and each setup gives you one along with a stop.

questions.q: In candle terms, what is a bullish kicker?
choices: A red candle, then a gap-up green one
A green candle, then a gap-down red one
One candle with a long lower wick
A small candle inside the prior range
questions.answer: A red candle, then a gap-up green one
questions.why: A red candle, then a gap-up green one. Investopedia: bullish kickers start with a bearish candle and then show a bullish gap up. Bulkowski's version is stricter: a tall black marubozu, an upward gap, then a tall white marubozu. The mirror image, a green candle then a gap-down red one, is the bearish kicker. One candle alone is never a kicker.
questions.lesson_line: Kicker: a down day, then a gap up going the other way.

wrong.A green candle, then a gap-down red one: That's the bearish kicker, the mirror image.
wrong.One candle with a long lower wick: One candle can't be a kicker. It takes two candles with a gap between them.
wrong.A small candle inside the prior range: A candle inside the day before has no gap. A kicker gaps away from the day before.

questions.simple: A bullish kicker is a red candle, then a green candle that gaps up, a sharp flip from down to up.

reasons: two Tier 2 publishers agree; stable definition

questions.q: In our setup list, what is an Oops Reversal?
choices: A gap up the day after a red day
A close back over a 4-day high average
A close out of a tight MA cluster
questions.why: The prior close, reclaimed intraday. The stock trades under yesterday's close, then gets back over it during the day. That reclaim is the entry. The plan then sells a third at 3R and a third at 5R and trails under each higher low. It is not the Kicker, which gaps up after a red day.
questions.lesson_line: Oops: it lost the prior close and took it back the same day.

wrong.A close back over a 4-day high average: That's the Slingshot's entry: the close back over the 4-day average of the highs.
wrong.A gap up the day after a red day: That's the Kicker: a red day, then a gap up the next day.

questions.simple: An Oops Reversal is a stock that drops under yesterday's close and then climbs back over it the same day.

reasons: house definition from TRADE_PLANS.md; stable

questions.q: What is a Launchpad in our setup list?
choices: A close out of a tight MA cluster
A close back over a 4-day high average
A pullback that holds an old gap
A weak open that buyers turn up
questions.answer: A close out of a tight MA cluster
questions.why: A close out of a tight MA cluster. The moving averages squeeze together, and the entry is the close that breaks out of the cluster. The stop sits under the 21-day and 50-day averages, a quarter of an ATR below the lower one. It is not the Slingshot, whose line is the 4-day average of the highs.
questions.lesson_line: Launchpad: averages squeezed together, then price closes out of the squeeze.

wrong.A close back over a 4-day high average: That's the Slingshot. Its line is a short average of the highs, not a cluster.
wrong.A pullback that holds an old gap: That's Gap Support: we buy the close as the gap holds.

questions.simple: A Launchpad is when the moving averages bunch up tight and price then closes out of that bunch.

reasons: house definition from TRADE_PLANS.md; stable

questions.q: What is Gap Support in our setup list?
choices: Buying a pullback that holds a gap
Shorting a gap down off the highs
Buying the open of any gap up
Waiting for a gap to fill, then buying
questions.answer: Buying a pullback that holds a gap
questions.why: Buying a pullback that holds a gap. The stock gaps up and runs, then comes back to the gap and holds. We buy the close as it holds. The stop is the gap top or the day's low, whichever is lower. If it drifts sideways at the gap, the stop tightens to just under the gap top. It is not buying the open of a fresh gap, and it does not wait for the gap to fill.
questions.lesson_line: Gap Support: the gap holds, you buy, and the gap is your line.

wrong.Shorting a gap down off the highs: Gap Support buys. A short off a gap down is the Bear gap lesson, and that one is measured, not traded.
wrong.Buying the open of any gap up: Gap Support waits for the gap to prove it holds. The entry is the close.
wrong.Waiting for a gap to fill, then buying: Our entry is the close while the gap still holds, not after it fills.

questions.simple: Gap Support means buying when a stock pulls back to an old gap and the gap holds.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: Our catalog lists HVC with the High Volume Edge. What does that setup enter on?
choices: The close of a high-volume day
The highest price of the day
A high-volume gap at the open
questions.answer: The close of a high-volume day
questions.why: The close of a high-volume day. Our catalog files HVC with the High Volume Edge, and that setup's entry is the high-volume close. The entry is a price. It is not a volume reading, a gap, or the day's high.
questions.lesson_line: High Volume Edge: the entry is where the heavy-volume day closed.

wrong.The highest price of the day: That's the high. Our entry is the high-volume close.
wrong.A high-volume gap at the open: It isn't about a gap. Our entry is where the heavy-volume day closed.
wrong.Volume above its 50-day average: That's a volume reading, not a price. Our entry is the close of that heavy day.

questions.simple: The High Volume Edge enters at the close of a heavy-volume day, not at its high or on a volume reading.

reasons: the HVC expansion has no citable house quote (owner flag)
fixed before

questions.q: What is our Go Signal?
choices: A weak open that buyers turn back up
A gap up the day after a red day
A pullback that holds an older gap up
A close out of a tight MA cluster
questions.answer: A weak open that buyers turn back up
questions.why: A weak open that buyers turn back up. It is an intraday entry in a stock that has already shown it can move. The day opens under the prior close. The low sweeps a nearby support. Then buyers step in and turn it.
questions.lesson_line: Go Signal: a strong stock opens weak, flushes support, and buyers turn it.

wrong.A gap up the day after a red day: That's the Kicker: a red day, then a gap up the next day.
wrong.A pullback that holds an older gap up: That's Gap Support: we buy the close as the gap holds.

questions.simple: The Go Signal is a strong stock that opens weak, dips through support, and then buyers turn it back up.

reasons: house definition from TRADE_PLANS.md; stable

questions.q: Which of our setups enters on the close back over the 4-day average of the highs?
questions.why: Slingshot. The stock slips under the 4-day average of the highs, then closes back over it, and that close is the entry. The Launchpad closes out of a cluster of averages. The Oops takes back the prior close during the day. The Go Signal turns a weak open back up intraday.
questions.lesson_line: Slingshot: back over the 4-day average of the highs, on the close.

wrong.Launchpad: The Launchpad closes out of a tight cluster of averages.
wrong.Oops Reversal: The Oops reclaims the prior close during the day.
wrong.Go Signal: The Go Signal turns a weak open back up during the day.

questions.simple: The Slingshot enters when the stock closes back over the 4-day average of the highs after slipping under it.

reasons: house definition; stable

questions.q: Our Oops Reversal plan puts the stop just under the day's low.
questions.why: True. The entry is the prior close, reclaimed during the day, and the plan's stop is the day's low. Our rulebook puts the stop order a few cents under that low, not exactly on it. So the stop sits just under the day's low.
questions.lesson_line: Oops: buy the reclaim, stop a few cents under the day's low.
questions.simple: True, the Oops Reversal stop goes a few cents under the low of the day you buy the reclaim.

questions.q: Fill in our line on holding winners.
questions.sentence: Hold your winners by selling ___ into strength and trailing the rising moving averages.
questions.why: Partials. You sell some of the position into strength, not all of it. The rest stays on, with the stop trailing the rising moving averages. Our sizes: a third at 3R, another third at 5R, then trail the last third. Selling everything at the first pop, or half at once, is not our line.
questions.lesson_line: Sell partials into strength. Trail the rest.

wrong.everything: Selling it all at the first pop ends the trade. The line keeps part of it on and trails it.
wrong.half: Our first trim is a third at 3R, not half.
wrong.losers: This line is about winners: take some off into strength and trail the rest.

questions.simple: Partials, because you sell part of a winner as it rises and keep the rest on with a trailing stop.

reasons: rests on the owner's own words and rulebook (E51)
